standard.title: Images add and multiply meaning
standard.description: understand that images add to or multiply the meanings of a text
standard.prior_knowledge: Students compare how images in different text types contribute to meaning (AC9E1LA08). They have not yet distinguished between images that add new information not in the written text versus images that multiply meaning by amplifying what the written text already expresses.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can understand that images add new meaning to a text or multiply existing meaning by amplifying what the written text expresses.

nodes.label: Images add meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify an image in a text that adds information not present in the written text and explain what new meaning the image provides.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one image in a text that provides information not stated in the written text and explain what new information the image adds.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and discuss multiple examples of images that add meaning in factual and narrative texts — maps, tables, illustrations showing setting — distinguishing what comes from the image alone vs the written text.
wider: Compare a factual text with its images removed and discuss what information is lost or becomes unclear
Identify images in digital texts (infographics, diagrams) that carry information the body text does not — and discuss why this division of information is used
success_criteria: Student can identify an image and state at least one piece of information it provides that is not in the written text.
Student can distinguish between what the image adds and what the written text says.

nodes.label: Images multiply meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify an image that amplifies or extends the meaning of accompanying words — showing emotion, atmosphere or subtext that the words alone do not fully convey.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify an illustration in a narrative that shows a character's emotion or reaction and explain how it extends what the words say.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and discuss multiple examples of images that multiply meaning in narratives — characters' actions, reactions, speech bubbles, thought processes — and explain what each adds beyond the written text.
wider: Compare how the same event is represented in the words and the illustration of a picture book and discuss where the image extends, contradicts or enriches the written meaning
Identify an image whose meaning changes depending on the surrounding words — and discuss how the combination creates meaning neither could alone

response_modes.reason: Students often see illustration as merely decoration or as 'showing what the words say'. The multiply-meaning concept — where the image goes further than the text — is counterintuitive. Multiple narrative examples with different kinds of amplification (emotion, irony, subtext) resolve this. More picture-book examples across different image-text relationships is the productive move.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The image-text relationship in picture books is a genuinely rich area for Year 2. Contradictory or ironic image-text relationships (where the image complicates the words) represent meaningful enrichment. Advancing students can begin to understand multimodal meaning-making at a level that has real literary depth.
success_criteria: Student can identify an image that amplifies or extends the words and explain what additional meaning the image creates.
Student does not describe the image as merely 'showing the same thing' when it does more than this.

nodes.label: Add and multiply across text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify whether images in a given text are adding new meaning or multiplying existing meaning, across both factual and narrative texts.
nodes.minimum_width: For a given text, classify at least one image as 'adding' and one as 'multiplying' and explain each.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse several texts across factual and narrative genres, identifying instances of images adding meaning and images multiplying meaning, and explain the role of each image in relation to the written text.
wider: Compare the roles of images across a picture book (narrative), an information report and a digital news article — discussing how each text type uses images differently
Create a two-image storyboard where one image adds meaning and one multiplies it, explaining the distinction

response_modes.reason: Applying both concepts — adding and multiplying — simultaneously to a range of texts requires coordinating the two distinctions. The integration demand is in holding both concepts active while reading.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one image that adds meaning and explain what new information it provides.
Student can identify at least one image that multiplies meaning and explain how it extends what the words say.
